title: Independent 2023-season verification finds GraphCast and three peer AI models match the best operational cyclone track models
summary: CIRA/Colorado State evaluation: GraphCast and three AI models match top operational cyclone track models in 2023; adding all four cut consensus error 11% at 120 h.
account: Google DeepMind's GraphCast was run live on ECMWF's public charts from 2023. DeepMind's blog of 14 November 2023 says the live model predicted Hurricane Lee's landfall in Nova Scotia in September 2023 about nine days in advance. The blog says only “In September”, so the year is implied by its 14 November 2023 post date. The ECMWF publications read do not document the case. MIT Technology Review quoted ECMWF's Peter Dueben saying the models are so good they cannot be avoided. An independent CIRA/Colorado State evaluation applied NHC verification to May-November 2023 cyclones. It found GraphCast-operational and three other AI models' track errors comparable to the best operational models. Adding all four improved the NHC track consensus by 11% at 120 h.
purpose: Medium-range global weather forecasting by machine learning, including severe-event prediction such as tropical cyclone tracks.
system: GraphCast (graph neural network global weather model)
model_version: GraphCast live experimental run on ECMWF charts (2023); GraphCast-operational in the CIRA evaluation
deployer: ECMWF (experimental live runs on public charts); CIRA/Colorado State University (evaluation)
segment: Meteorological research and operational forecast centers

paired_incident.basis: Google's AI-based earthquake alert system underestimated hazard magnitude; same developer family and hazard-prediction task as DeepMind's GraphCast cyclone forecasts, harming the exposed public.

headline: GraphCast matches best operational cyclone track models in 2023
metric: adding all four improved the NHC track consensus by 11% at 120 h

comparator.against: the NHC track consensus without the four AI models, benchmarked against the long-term improvement of official forecasts
comparator.before: consensus track errors without the AIWP models; official five-day track forecasts improving by about 2% per year since 2001
comparator.after: consensus track errors reduced by up to 11% at the longer time periods
comparator.quote: The consensus track errors are reduced by up to 11% at the longer time periods. The five-day NHC official track forecasts have improved by about 2% per year since 2001, so this represents more than a five-year gain in accuracy.

later.note: By the 2025 season NHC had brought AI-based models, including a newer Google DeepMind ensemble, into real-time operations, per its verification report.
later.quote: The 2025 season marked the first time that NHC incorporated AI-based models into real-time operations.
